logic_validation.anti_cheat: The trace is strictly READ-ONLY of state the query already computed (sims / decoded words / matched index were computed regardless; cp_rf_fired/v/u are the resonate's OUTPUT). NO extra resonate, NO extra GPU work per turn. The answer + the no-confab moat are UNCHANGED (the abstain code path is the same; the trace only RECORDS the abstain, never supplies a fallback).

honest_notes: NO extra resonate was needed -- the gauge reads cp_rf_fired/|Z| off the cached _resonate bridge (rf) or the shared bridge's rf slice (onebrain), both already produced by the query. The per-role CONFIDENCE for the rf cue roles does one extra unbind+matched-filter over the matched block (read-only, the same op the cleanup uses), but ONLY on the trace path and ONLY for the single matched block -- not per-turn GPU bloat across all facts.

|Z| (mean recovery magnitude) is unbounded (it scales with the kick magnitude, e.g. ~36 for rf D=64, ~10k for onebrain): the gauge BAR clamps to [0,1] for display but the LABEL shows the true value. frac_fired is a true fraction in [0,1].

OneBrain `_block_role_scores` confidence is the winner/peak margin (1.0 on a confident match); the rf `_cleanup_all_scored` confidence is the raw mean-cos. Both are documented in the helper docstrings; they're not directly comparable across composers but each is a faithful per-composer 'how confident' read.

The webapp's chat brains (tiny-demo / self-knowledge / developed bundles via composer_kind='rf') use the RFPhasorComposer, so the rf trace is the live path; the onebrain trace is wired for parity (composer_kind='onebrain').
